_note: Fixture plans for the explain_query_plan tool. They are hand-written in PostgreSQL 16 EXPLAIN (ANALYZE off) format against the schema in sample-app/src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__init.sql with about 50,000 synthetic observation rows. They are NOT captured from a live database; they exist so an agent can reason about index use without database access.

observation-by-subject-and-code.sql: select o.* from observation o where o.patient_id = ? and o.code = ? order by o.effective_date_time desc
plan: ->  Index Scan using ix_observation_patient_code on observation o  (cost=0.29..12.57 rows=4 width=98)
notes: Uses the composite index ix_observation_patient_code (patient_id, code).
The sort is cheap because the index narrows the rows to one patient and one code.

observation-by-subject.sql: select o.* from observation o where o.patient_id = ? order by o.effective_date_time desc
plan: ->  Index Scan using ix_observation_patient_code on observation o  (cost=0.29..38.20 rows=92 width=98)
notes: Leading column patient_id of ix_observation_patient_code is usable on its own.
Loads the whole history of one patient; fine for a single search, wasteful when called in a loop.

lastn-per-subject-loop.sql: for each subject id: select p.* from patient p where p.id = ?; select o.* from observation o where o.patient_id = ? order by o.effective_date_time desc
plan: Index Scan using patient_pkey on patient p  (cost=0.28..8.29 rows=1 width=72)
->  Index Scan using ix_observation_patient_code on observation o  (cost=0.29..38.20 rows=92 width=98)
notes: Each plan is individually fine; the defect is the number of round trips (N+1 pattern).
500 subjects means about 1,000 statements and about 46,000 rows read to return 500 rows.

lastn-set-based-proposed.source: Proposed replacement for ObservationService.lastN (not in the sample app)
lastn-set-based-proposed.sql: select * from (select o.*, row_number() over (partition by o.patient_id order by o.effective_date_time desc) as rn from observation o where o.patient_id = any(?)) t where t.rn = 1
plan: Subquery Scan on t  (cost=402.10..437.60 rows=7 width=106)
->  Bitmap Heap Scan on observation o  (cost=31.12..330.40 rows=1380 width=98)
->  Bitmap Index Scan on ix_observation_patient_code  (cost=0.00..30.78 rows=1380 width=0)
notes: One statement regardless of the number of subjects.
An index on (patient_id, effective_date_time DESC) would remove the Sort; propose it as a new Flyway migration V2, never by editing V1.
